newsitem.title: UK: Turkey security zone violates Iraq territory--Iran.
newsitem.headline: Turkey security zone violates Iraq territory--Iran.

text.p: Iran said on Sunday that Turkey's proposed security zone in Iraq was a territorial violation that would escalate regional tensions.
The Ankara government's decision to create a security area was criticised by Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi, the Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
Iran believed such a zone violated Iraqi territorial integrity which had to be maintained.

Mohammadi said the Turkish move was "contrary to the good intentions of a neighbouring nation, in violation of international codes of practice and a measure not acceptable to the Islamic Republic of Iran".
He added that "such a measure would be the cause of an escalation of tension in the region", IRNA reported.
Iran earlier rejected accusations that its forces had intervened in fighting between Kurdish factions in northern Iraq.
Iranian television reported on Sunday that Tehran wanted a peaceful solution to the region's problems.

Baghdad has also warned northern neighbour Turkey since Ankara started a border military buildup in an apparent attempt to establish a five to 10 km (three to six mile) -wide cordon to deter attacks by rebel Turkish Kurds.
Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said on Saturday that Turkey might empty some settlements within the buffer zone.
Mohammadi also condemned a call by six Gulf Arab states on Sunday for Iran to end what they said was its occupation of three Gulf islands also claimed by the United Arab Emirates.

The spokesman said that the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) of Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and UAE was supposed to review the United States' missile attacks on Iraq in a meeting that had yielded no results.

A GCC statement issued after a two-day meeting of foreign ministers in Saudi Arabia said Iran was trying to maintain the "status quo by force" on the Abu Musa, Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb islands, which lie near key oil shipping lanes.
Mohammadi said that instead of passing a pre-judgment about sovereignty over the Iranian islands, the meeting should have advised the UAE to continue bilateral negotiations.
